sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay mechanics of House Above are surprisingly straightforward. Players take on the role of a house-thrower, tasked with tossing houses onto a growing tower without letting them fall. The game's controls are intuitive, allowing players to use their mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to throw houses with precision. The game's physics engine also adds a layer of realism, making it feel like the houses are actually floating in mid-air.

As players progress through the game, they'll encounter various obstacles, including uneven terrain, obstacles, and even other houses that can knock their own houses off balance. The game's increasing difficulty is what makes it so addictive, as players must adapt their throwing techniques to overcome each new challenge. The game also features a variety of house types, each with its own unique characteristics and throwing requirements.

One of the game's most surprising features is its use of luck. At times, the game's physics engine can be unpredictable, and a house might land perfectly, only to have another one fall off balance. This element of chance adds a thrilling layer of unpredictability to the game, making it feel fresh and exciting even after multiple playthroughs.

House Above's core gameplay mechanics are designed to be easy to learn but difficult to master. Players must develop their skills and adapt their throwing techniques to overcome each new challenge. With time and practice, players can unlock new levels and even compete with their friends to achieve the highest score.
